# `analysis swarm-reads` fixtures

One synthetic deployment carrying both arms of an ADR-0026 swarm run, with every
expected figure worked out on paper below. Synthetic on purpose, for the reason
the `browser-reads/` fixtures beside it are: the question here is arithmetic over
rows whose shape is already fixed by the two tables, so the useful fixture is one
whose every number can be checked by hand — which these can be.

Seven files:

| file | what |
| --- | --- |
| `native-rows.json` | `deployment_hot_file_download_records` as plain JSON — both arms, plus rows to ignore |
| `browser-rows.json` | `deployment_browser_download_records` — the swarm arm's browsers, plus one to ignore |
| `hot-file-config.json` | `deploy_args.hot_file_readers` — four native reader VMs with their parities |
| `browser-config.json` | `deploy_args.browser_downloaders` — the one browser VM |
| `hot-files.json` | the hot-file selection (one 300 MiB file, with its sha256) |
| `trace-docs.json` | Elasticsearch `_source` documents, as telegraf writes them |
| `get-rpc-responses.json` | one `get_rpc` aggregation response per round, keyed by round id |

`status` is its string value and `started_at` is ISO-8601; the tests feed the rows
to `saorsa_deploy.swarm_reads` as dicts.

All of it is built on **period 600 s** and round **R0 = 2987190**, whose boundary
is exactly `2026-10-18T09:00:00Z` (2987190 x 600 = 1792314000). Regenerated by
rebuilding the tables below; no generator is committed, because every value here
is stated rather than computed.

## The window and the rounds

The tests' window is `2026-10-18T09:00:00Z` → `2026-10-18T10:00:00Z`, half-open,
which is **six rounds**: R0..R0+5. Even rounds are the swarm arm's, odd ones the
control arm's.

| round | boundary | arm | rows |
| --: | --- | --- | --- |
| 2987190 | 09:00Z | swarm | 4 native (all ok), 2 browser (all ok) |
| 2987191 | 09:10Z | control | 4 native (all ok) — **plus one off-parity swarm BROWSER row** |
| 2987192 | 09:20Z | swarm | 4 native (3 ok, 1 `timeout`), 2 browser (1 ok, 1 `skipped`) |
| 2987193 | 09:30Z | control | 4 native (3 ok, 1 `connection`) |
| 2987194 | 09:40Z | swarm | none — **missing** |
| 2987195 | 09:50Z | control | none — **missing** |

So four rounds carry rows and two are missing, one in each arm. Narrowing the
window to `09:30Z` leaves R0..R0+2 — two present swarm rounds and **one** present
control round — which is the G3 NOT ASSESSED case.

## The cohorts

* **swarm** (extension `swarm`, `round_parity: even`) — two native reader VMs,
  `...-hot-file-read-lon1-1` and `...-hot-file-read-nyc3-1`, two instances each;
  one browser VM `...-browser-download-lon1-1`, two instances.
* **control** (extension `control`, `round_parity: odd`) — two native reader VMs,
  two instances each. No browser.

Ignored rows: two of extension `other`, one with **no extension at all** (the
deployment's own tier), and one `other` browser row — **4 ignored**.

The off-parity row is a `swarm` **browser** row on round 2987191, a control
round. It is **counted** (`off_parity_rows: 1`) and is in **none** of the
figures: not in the swarm arm's summary, because `rows_of_arm` keeps only the
even rounds, and not in the control arm's, because that arm is the `control`
extension. Its own trace records are the two `chunk-z` documents described
below, which the chunk set excludes for the same reason.

**A browser is the only role an off-parity row is legal for.** A native reader on
the other arm's rounds is refused outright — by `check_parities` on the recorded
config (`round_parity: all` included) and by `check_native_round_parity` on the
rows — because a `get_rpc` document names a chunk, a time and a node and never
the cohort that asked, so such a reader's GETs land inside the other arm's round
windows where nothing can separate them. A browser emits no `get_rpc` at all.

## Native rows, round by round

### Swarm, round 2987190 — four readers, all successful, all with peers

| host | inst | total_ms | records_from_peers | bytes_from_peers | records_served | bytes_served | verify |
| --- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| lon1-1 | 1 | 10,000 | 40 | 4,000,000 | 10 | 1,000,000 | 0 |
| lon1-1 | 2 | 12,000 | 60 | 6,000,000 | 20 | 2,000,000 | 0 |
| nyc3-1 | 1 | 14,000 | 20 | 2,000,000 | 5 | 500,000 | 0 |
| nyc3-1 | 2 | 16,000 | 10 | 1,000,000 | 5 | 500,000 | 0 |

completion 4/4 = **100%**; peer share 4/4 = **100%**; p50 **13,000 ms**
(`[10,12,14,16]` k → (12+14)/2); p95 **15,700 ms** (0.95 x 3 = 2.85, so
14,000 x 0.15 + 16,000 x 0.85).

### Swarm, round 2987192 — one timeout, one reader with no peer record

| host | inst | status | total_ms | from_peers | bytes_from_peers | served | bytes_served | verify |
| --- | --: | --- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| lon1-1 | 1 | success | 11,000 | 50 | 5,000,000 | 10 | 1,000,000 | 0 |
| lon1-1 | 2 | success | 13,000 | 30 | 3,000,000 | 10 | 1,000,000 | 1 |
| nyc3-1 | 1 | success | 15,000 | 10 | 1,000,000 | 0 | 0 | 2 |
| nyc3-1 | 2 | failure `timeout` | — | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | — |

completion 3/4 = **75%**; peer share 3/4 = **75%** (the failure took nothing from
a peer, and a failed read is still an attempt); p50 **13,000 ms**; p95
**14,800 ms** (0.95 x 2 = 1.9 over `[11,13,15]` k).

`verify_status` is one of each: 1 mismatch, 1 ok, 1 unchecked. **2 is not a
failure** — a selection line with no SHA-256 leaves nothing to verify.

### Swarm arm over both rounds (8 rows)

* attempted 8, success 7, failure 1, skipped 0 → completion **7/8 = 87.5%**
* rows with peers 7 → peer share **87.5%**
* sums: `records_from_peers` **220**, `bytes_from_peers` **22,000,000**,
  `records_served` **60**, `bytes_served` **6,000,000**
* per-row medians over the 8 attempted rows:
  `records_from_peers` sorted `[0,10,10,20,30,40,50,60]` → **25**;
  `bytes_from_peers` → **2,500,000**;
  `records_served` `[0,0,5,5,10,10,10,20]` → **7.5**;
  `bytes_served` → **750,000**
* p50 **13,000 ms** over the 7 successes `[10,11,12,13,14,15,16]` k; p95
  **15,700 ms** (0.95 x 6 = 5.7)
* verify: mismatch **1**, ok **5**, unchecked **1**
* `swarm_present`: true **8**
* discovery totals: every row carries `announces=2, refused=0, timed_out=0,
  offers_made=3, offers_delivered=3, links_proven=3, links_failed=0` except the
  timed-out one, which carries `announces=2, refused=1, timed_out=1,
  offers_made=1, offers_delivered=0, links_proven=0, links_failed=1`. So
  announces **16**, refused **1**, timed_out **1**, offers_made **22**,
  offers_delivered **21**, links_proven **21**, links_failed **1**.

### Control arm (8 rows over 2987191 and 2987193)

Four readers per round at 30/32/34/36 k and 31/33/35 k plus one `connection`
failure. Every swarm counter is **0** and `swarm_present` is **false** on all
eight — which is what a released `ant` produces, and the flag is what makes those
zeros readable.

* completion **7/8 = 87.5%**; peer share **0%**
* p50 **33,000 ms** over `[30,31,32,33,34,35,36]` k; p95 **35,700 ms**
* `unexpected_swarm_rows` **0**

## Browser rows (extension `swarm`)

| round | inst | status | total_ms | from_peers | bytes_from_peers | served | bytes_served | chunks total/nodes/cache/readers |
| --: | --: | --- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --- |
| 2987190 | 1 | success | 20,000 | 100 | 10,000,000 | 50 | 5,000,000 | 300/100/0/200 |
| 2987190 | 2 | success | 24,000 | 80 | 8,000,000 | 40 | 4,000,000 | 300/150/0/150 |
| 2987192 | 1 | success | 22,000 | 60 | 6,000,000 | 30 | 3,000,000 | 300/120/0/180 |
| 2987192 | 2 | skipped `round_overrun` | — | — | — | — | — | — |

The skipped row carries **no counter at all** (every one NULL), because a round
that launched no browser cannot have had a swarm and a 0 there would read as one
that formed and shared nothing.

* rows 4, attempted 3, success 3, skipped 1 → completion **100%**
* peer share **3/3 = 100%**
* sums: from_peers **240**, bytes **24,000,000**, served **120**, bytes_served
  **12,000,000**; medians **80**, **8,000,000**, **40**, **4,000,000**
* chunk sources: total **900**, nodes **370**, cache **0**, readers **530**
* p50 **22,000 ms**, p95 **23,800 ms** (0.95 x 2 = 1.9 over `[20,22,24]` k)
* `swarm_present`: true **3**, null **1**

## `trace-docs.json` — the chunk set and the browsers' GETs

22 documents, each an ES `_source` with the fields nested under `browser_trace`
and the tags under `tag`, exactly as telegraf writes them.

Round 2987190, both instances of the swarm cohort's browser VM, in `seq` order:

| chunk | records |
| --- | --- |
| chunk-a | `start`/`finish found 1024 bytes` to `12D3KooWA0` |
| chunk-b | `start`/`finish NotFound` to a bootstrap seed, then `start`/`finish found` to `12D3KooWB0` |
| chunk-c | `start`/`finish found` to `12D3KooWC0` |

That is 8 records per download, so **16**. Round 2987192's single surviving
instance reads chunk-a and **chunk-d** (`found` each) — **4** more. Two final
documents sit on round **2987191**, a CONTROL round, naming `chunk-z`: they are
the off-parity browser row's own trace, and they prove the chunk set is taken
from the swarm rounds alone and that the browsers' own GET counts exclude them.

Every document carries the swarm cohort's browser hostname, because the trace
query names that cohort's VMs as well as its rounds: a second browser extension
reading in the same rounds would otherwise put its targets into this file's
record set, and that set is the filter the fleet's GETs are counted through.

* chunk set: **4** records — `chunk-a`, `chunk-b`, `chunk-c`, `chunk-d` — from
  rounds **2987190, 2987192**. `chunk-z` is NOT in it.
* browsers' GETs: round 2987190 → 2 downloads, **6** found, **2** NotFound (3.00
  and 1.00 per download); round 2987192 → 1 download, **2** found, **0** NotFound.
  Over the window: 3 downloads, **8** found, **2** NotFound → **2.67** and
  **0.67** per download.

## `get-rpc-responses.json` — the fleet's GETs for the file

One aggregation response per round, in the shape
`parse_get_rpc_response` reads: `hits.total.value`, a `requests` terms
aggregation, a `storage_outcomes` terms aggregation with a nested `latency`
percentiles aggregation, and a `hosts` terms aggregation.

| round | arm | served | not_found | total | get | get_or_closer | NODE-1 | NODE-2 | NODE-3 |
| --: | --- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| 2987190 | swarm | 200 | 50 | 250 | 200 | 50 | 120 | 80 | 50 |
| 2987191 | control | 400 | 100 | 500 | 450 | 50 | 250 | 150 | 100 |
| 2987192 | swarm | 240 | 60 | 300 | 250 | 50 | 150 | 100 | 50 |
| 2987193 | control | 440 | 110 | 550 | 500 | 50 | 300 | 150 | 100 |
| 2987194 | swarm | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | — | — | — |
| 2987195 | control | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | — | — | — |

The two missing rounds still have a response — the command queries every round in
the window — and it is **empty**, which is also the point: those rounds are
excluded from the medians by being MISSING, not by their GET count.

**The medians are over each arm's COMPARABLE rounds**, which here are its present
ones: every present round has four attempted native rows. A round is comparable
only if its arm attempted a native read in it and the GETs could be counted,
because the figure counts what the nodes served to NATIVE readers — so a round
whose readers all `skipped` is present and not comparable. The tests build that
case by flipping round 2987193's control rows to `skipped`: the round keeps its
440 served GETs, leaves the median, and takes the control arm below G3's
two-round minimum.

* served median, swarm arm: median of `[200, 240]` = **220**
* served median, control arm: median of `[400, 440]` = **420**
* **G3 ratio 220 / 420 = 0.524**
* total medians: swarm **275**, control **525**
* busiest hosts over the window: NODE-1 **820**, NODE-2 **480**, NODE-3 **300**
  (summing to 1,600 = 250 + 500 + 300 + 550)

## The gates

At the tests' thresholds — `min_completion 0.85`, `min_peer_share 0.70`,
`max_get_ratio 0.80` — every gate passes and the verdict is **PASS**:

| gate | figure | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| G1 completion | swarm native 87.50%, control native 87.50%, swarm browser 100.00% | PASS |
| G2 swarms form | worst round 2987192 native at 75.0% | PASS |
| G3 nodes relieved | 0.524 (swarm 220 / control 420) | PASS |
| G4 no slower | swarm 13,000 ms vs control 33,000 ms (-60.6%) | PASS |

Each one fails against a threshold the fixture's own figures are below — G1 at the
command's default 0.95 (87.5% < 95%), G2 at 0.80 (75% < 80%), G3 at 0.50
(0.524 > 0.50) — which is also how the tests prove the thresholds are wired
rather than decorative.

**G1 and G2 are NOT ASSESSED rather than PASS when a required figure is
absent**, since "three figures, all must pass" is not satisfied by two. The tests
build those cases by dropping the browser rows (G1's third figure, and G2's
browser share in each swarm round) or by flipping a swarm round's native rows to
`skipped`. A real breach still outranks the absence and FAILs, because a FAIL is
knowledge.
